title: His brother Paul, drummer and sound-effects man in Hollywood
summary: DeDroit describes his brother Paul, a drummer and marimba player who worked with Alfred Newman and later in cartoon sound effects.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well, my father was a musician, my brother was the greatest drummer I ever lived. He was with Alfred Newman for many years. And Hollywood. I have the red book that Soussone got out, it says that he played in the pit at the Orphiom and with his brother Johnny's band. He was the greatest woodpile man on the Pacific coast. You know the woodpile, the marimbas, huh? And he had Georgia the drum section. He made enough money to retire in three figures. He had the drawing account $15,000 a year if he never had a note. But he knew the business. He started with Flip the Frog, the cartoons. They eventually went out of business, but my brother got to be quite a sound effect man. He was a great band and he loved learning his own. In addition to being a great drummer, because he played big time at 16, he was also a trombonist. And he could read all the clefs and all the keys. He was a musician.
I didn't know he was a trombonist.
